data.title: RDGA Nameserver Clustering Anomaly
data.description: Detects disproportionate concentration of newly registered domains pointing to the same nameserver infrastructure within a 24-hour window. RDGA operators typically provision hundreds or thousands of domains but anchor them to a small set of nameservers they control, creating a fan-in pattern that is statistically anomalous compared to legitimate registrar or hosting provider distributions. Legitimate nameservers serving large numbers of new domains tend to be well-known hosting or registrar nameservers with established reputation. This rule identifies nameserver endpoints receiving an abnormal influx of newly registered domain delegations, filtering out known hosting infrastructure. Supports TP-0041 Phase 2 detection of RDGA nameserver infrastructure consolidation.

detection.condition: selection and aggregation and not exclusion

falsepositives: New hosting providers onboarding large customer bases rapidly
DNS migration events where many domains switch nameservers simultaneously
Reseller registrars consolidating domains under shared nameserver infrastructure
